words.explanation: n. [U] friendly behavior toward visitors 好客；殷勤
words.example: We were delighted by the wonderful hospitality of the local people.

words.explanation: vi. to feel very embarrassed or ashamed 感到尴尬；局促不安
words.example: The little girl squirmed with shyness in front of strangers.

words.explanation: n. [U] ( fml. ) a way of behaving that people consider to be correct（行为的）恰当，得体
words.example: By the end of the semester, students will have learned the nicety of table manners.

words.explanation: vt. ( usu. passive ) ( be / feel ~d to do sth. ) to make sb. feel that it is necessary to do sth. 迫使；使（某人）负有义务
words.example: We feel obliged to ask him to dinner.

words.explanation: n. [C] ( fml. ) sth. that represents a feeling, fact, event, etc. 象征；标志
words.example: Please accept this bunch of ﬂowers as a small token of our thanks.

words.explanation: n. [U] a feeling of being grateful to sb. for sth. 感激；感谢
words.example: We want to invite you to dinner in appreciation of your hard work this week.

words.explanation: n. [C] a meal to which each guest brings some food, which is then shared out among the guests 百味餐（参加者带食物分享）
a. relaxed and friendly without being restricted by rules of correct behavior 轻松友好的；不拘礼节的
words.example: The two families met for informal talks.

words.explanation: a. not formal, or not for a formal situation 非正式的；不拘礼节的；休闲的；便装的
words.example: His casual clothes were not appropriate for such a formal occasion.

words.explanation: vt. to formally or officially tell sb. about sth. or give them information（正式）通知，告知（某人）
words.example: The bank never informed us of how the money was being invested.

words.explanation: n. [U] a situation in which sth. does not happen when it should 推迟；延期
words.example: I hope that our discussions will take place without delay.

words.explanation: a. usual in a particular society or situation 惯常的；合乎习俗的
words.example: It is customary to wear new clothing for the Chinese New Year.

words.explanation: vt. to say sth. nice to sb. in order to praise them 赞美；恭维
words.example: His parents seldom complimented him on his good grades.

words.explanation: n. [C, U] sweet food served after the main part of a meal（饭后的）甜食，甜品，甜点
n. [U] ( infml. ) conversation about things that are not very important 聊天；闲谈
words.example: The international negotiations begin with chit-chat.

words.explanation: vi. to secretly try to get information that sb. would not want you to have 探听；窥探
words.example: Somebody went snooping through my drawer while I was gone.

words.explanation: n. [C] a party that you give to celebrate when you have just moved into a new house 庆祝乔迁聚会
a. happening without anyone expecting or knowing about it 未经通报的；出人意料的
words.example: He paid an unannounced visit and that was a big surprise.

words.explanation: n. [C]（手的）拇指
n. [C] sth. difficult or worrying that you are responsible for 重担；负担
words.example: I don't want to be a burden on my team with my painful feet.

words.explanation: n. [C] ( infml. ) an annoying person, esp. a child 令人讨厌的人（尤指孩子）；讨厌鬼
vi. to be grateful for sth. sb. has done 感激
words.example: I don't need any help, but I do appreciate your kind oﬀer.

words.explanation: a. friendly, welcoming, and generous to visitors 好客的；殷勤的；热情友好的
words.example: Chinese citizens are some of the most hospitable people.

words.explanation: n. [pl.] ( also ~s ) ( infml. ) people 人；人们
words.example: Folks around here are pretty friendly.

words.explanation: v. to receive sb. as a guest and give them food and drink or other forms often joyment 招待；款待；请客
words.example: My father got home late tonight as he needed to entertain some business clients.

words.explanation: a. famous and admired 非常有名的；大名鼎鼎的
words.example: He is legendary for his courage and strategy.

words.explanation: n. [C] a small piece of thick rough material that covers part of a floor 地垫；地席；蒲席
vt. to clean sth. by rubbing it against a surface 擦干净（某物）
words.example: Please wipe your feet before you come in.

words.explanation: to feel relaxed and comfortable in a particular place or situation 舒适自在；无拘束
words.example: The kind hosts did everything they could to make the guests feel at home.

words.explanation: arriving at the correct time and not late 准时；按时
words.example: They have to work overtime to get the job done on time.

words.explanation: used when saying what another possibility might be 要不；否则
words.example: You can get a new set of tools, or else you may use mine for the time being.

words.explanation: to stay with sb. longer than they want you to 呆得太久而不再受欢迎
words.example: Jack visited the Smiths so often that he wore out his welcome.

words.explanation: used to emphasize that sth. is more important than the other things you have already mentioned 尤其是；最重要的是
words.example: Above all, parents want their children to be happy.

words.explanation: to visit sb. when you have not arranged to come at a particular time 顺便造访；临时拜访
words.example: I'll drop by on my way home if I have time.

words.explanation: a rule you use for doing or explaining things that is based on experience 经验之谈；经验法则
words.example: A good rule of thumb is to think twice before you take action.

words.word: for days / weeks, etc. at a time
words.explanation: continuously for a period of several days / weeks, etc. 持续几天/几周等
words.example: Dad has been very busy recently and may be gone for six days at a time.
words.phonetic: for days  weeks, etc. at a time.mp3

words.explanation: especially 尤其；特别
words.example: There's one thing in particular I want for my birthday, a box of chocolates.

words.word: welcome / greet sb. / sth. with open arms
words.explanation: to bevery pleased to see sb. or sth. 热烈地欢迎/迎接某人/某事物
words.example: When my uncle came to visit us at Christmas, we welcomed him with open arms.
words.phonetic: welcome  greet sb.  sth. with open arms.mp3
